title: Associate Manager - Quality Compliance
jobDescription:

Our science and risk-based compliant quality culture is both flexible and innovative, always putting the patient first. Your contributions will be vital and will have a direct impact on patient care, ensuring we deliver on our promise of quality and safety.

QUALIFICATIONS:
Education Bachelor's or Master's Degree in Pharmacy, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Life Sciences, Chemistry, Biotechnology, Microbiology, or a related discipline. Experience: 8–12 years of experience in Quality Assurance, Quality Compliance, Data Integrity, Market Complaints, or Quality Systems within the pharmaceutical industry. Experience in regulated sterile manufacturing environments. Exposure to global regulatory inspections (US FDA, MHRA, EMA, WHO, TGA, Health Canada, etc.). Experience with e QMS, laboratory systems, and manufacturing systems is preferred. Data Integrity Management Partner with the Site Data Integrity Lead to promote good data management practices and a strong Data Integrity culture across Gx P functions. Support implementation and maintenance of Data Integrity Governance programs in line with regulatory and corporate requirements. Conduct periodic Data Integrity walkthroughs in Manufacturing, QC Laboratories, Warehouses, Utilities, Engineering, and other GMP areas. Identify gaps related to ALCOA principles and drive appropriate CAPA implementation. Perform periodic reviews of manufacturing and laboratory operations for Data Integrity compliance. Support development of Data Governance processes, procedures, training programs, and awareness initiatives. Monitor effectiveness of Data Integrity controls and remediation activities. Participate in site and global Data Integrity forums to share best practices and continuous improvement initiatives. Investigations & Compliance Participate in investigations related to Data Integrity concerns, compliance issues, and improper practices. Conduct root cause analysis and support development of effective CAPAs. Review CAPAs for adequacy, effectiveness, and timely implementation. title: Marketing Channel Delivery Manager, EM MISP Cluster Markets
jobDescription:
Role Purpose: The Global Operations Services Center (GOSC) is seeking a highly motivated Marketing Channel Delivery Manager to lead marketing channel and samples services for Pfizer's International Markets in Malaysia, Indonesia, Singapore and the Philippines. In this role, you will partner directly with local brand and marketing teams, BOPs, Digital and Commercial Excellence & Innovation teams to develop digital and samples strategies that meet the needs of HCPs and patients, in adherence with global standards, compliance, legal and business requirements, on time and to budget. You will serve as a trusted advisor to your markets and work closely with the GOSC Delivery team to ensure the successful implementation of these services. Beyond your assigned markets, you will contribute to broader GOSC initiatives, driving innovation, continuous improvement and best practices. In particular, the Marketing Channel Delivery Manager will focus on: Samples Management for a high-volume, multi-market samples operation: annual sample plans, monitoring plans and work instructions, warehouse and logistics provider oversight, audit readiness and deviation management, ensuring compliance and efficiency. Campaign Management capabilities through the planning and oversight of outbound (email) marketing programs, from brief to performance review. HCP Portal (Pfizer Pro) to engage customers with promotional messaging and access to Pfizer products and services. Advise marketing teams on portal strategy to enhance the customer experience, including portal governance and above-brand oversight. Social 2-way Communications rollout, oversight and scale, ensuring process execution, compliance and efficiency. e Permission governance to support the customer acquisition strategy (collection, management, data quality and reporting). Omnichannel reporting management and oversight to measure omnichannel performance and guarantee KPI consistency across global standard dashboards. Main Role

RESPONSIBILITIES:
Develop strong relationships with local brand, marketing and customer-facing teams, gaining a deep understanding of each market's priorities, customers and channel needs. Build and maintain a clear plan per market, agreed with local business leaders, defining where Marketing Channel Delivery services add most value and how success will be measured. Translate global standards, platform changes and new capabilities into clear, actionable plans for your markets, driving adoption, compliance and consistent ways of working. Partner with the GOSC Delivery team to ensure timely, accurate and effective execution of channel and samples services: define requirements and quality expectations, monitor service levels and manage escalations to resolution. Collaborate effectively across Marketing, Medical, Legal, Compliance, Digital, Centers of Excellence and other partner functions, ensuring approvals and compliance standards are met on time and to budget. Serve as a trusted advisor to omnichannel teams, recommending how to structure campaigns, portals and customer journeys that maximise value across touch points. Lead training and capability building for marketing and customer-facing colleagues on channel and samples platforms, processes and best practices. Use data, dashboards and KPIs to evaluate channel and samples performance, generate insights and oversee channel adoption Maintain audit readiness through accurate documentation and ensure adherence to all relevant policies, procedures and Legal and Compliance standards. Lead continuous improvement initiatives across GOSC, identifying opportunities for automation, simplification and AI-enabled ways of working, and driving best practices across international markets. Qualifications BA required; MBA or equivalent Master's-level education preferred. 5 -12 years of experience in Digital or Omnichannel marketing, Marketing operations or Commercial operations, ideally in the pharmaceutical, biotechnology or healthcare sector. Experience in medical samples management and its compliance requirements (sample plans, monitoring, audit readiness) is a strong advantage. Proven stakeholder management and influencing skills across multiple markets and functions, with the ability to build credibility and drive decisions without direct authority. Experience partnering with delivery teams or service providers to define requirements, manage quality and resolve escalations. Strong analytical skills, with the ability to work with metrics and KPIs and translate insights into action. Passion for digital innovation and AI, with a track record of simplifying or improving processes. High degree of ownership and agility, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and independently drive programs to completion. Fluent English required; additional regional languages are an advantage. Ability to work across Asia-Pacific time zones. title: Manager, Incentive Compensation
jobDescription: ROLE SUMMARY: The Global Operation Services Center (GOSC) is seeking a highly motivated Manager, Incentive Compensation Design to lead incentive compensation strategy and design for Pfizer's Tier 3 International Markets. In this role, you will partner directly with business leaders across diverse global markets to develop bonus plans, quota-setting methodologies, and recognition programs that motivate customer-facing colleagues and drive business performance. You will serve as a trusted advisor, translating business objectives into incentive compensation solutions that are simple, motivating, fiscally responsible, and compliant with Pfizer policies and governance standards. Working closely with the GOSC Delivery team, you will also lead the successful implementation and ongoing administration of these programs. This role combines strategic consulting, analytics, and stakeholder management. It is ideal for someone who thrives at the intersection of data and business strategy, enjoys solving complex performance challenges, and can confidently communicate recommendations to senior leaders. Success in this position requires both strong quantitative capabilities and the ability to influence decision-making through clear, evidence-based insights. Beyond supporting assigned markets, this role will contribute to broader GOSC strategic initiatives, driving innovation, continuous improvement, and best practices across international incentive compensation programs. ROLE RESPOSNSIBILITIES: Incentive Compensation Strategy & Design Design, enhance, and maintain incentive compensation plans aligned with local business strategies and commercial objectives. Develop and refine quota-setting methodologies that support performance, fairness, and business growth. Design local recognition and award programs that reinforce desired behaviors and strategic priorities. Partner with business leaders to identify challenges and proactively recommend incentive compensation solutions. Analytics & Strategic Consulting Analyze incentive compensation program effectiveness and identify opportunities for optimization. Leverage data and analytics to generate insights, evaluate program performance, and support strategic decision-making. Build robust business cases and recommendations for plan design changes, balancing motivation, affordability, and risk management. Serve as a trusted advisor to market leadership by providing objective, data-driven guidance. Stakeholder Partnership Develop strong relationships with market leaders and gain deep understanding of local business priorities, products, customer dynamics, and competitive landscapes. Facilitate discussions and influence stakeholders through credible recommendations and clear communication. Collaborate effectively across Commercial Excellence, Finance, PX, Compliance, and other partner functions. Program Implementation, Governance & Service Delivery Partner with GOSC Delivery teams to ensure timely, accurate, and effective implementation and administration of incentive compensation programs. Collaborate with GOSC to calculate bonus payouts, contests, awards, and field quotas using approved processes, tools, and templates. Ensure all incentive compensation deliverables are accurate, complete, and distributed to the field force according to established timelines. Own governance and operational oversight across all incentive compensation services within assigned markets. Create, maintain, and manage incentive compensation production calendars, ensuring alignment across business, operational, and support stakeholders. Hold stakeholders accountable for data ownership, validation, quality, and timely submission of required inputs. Implement new processes, tools, and initiatives in alignment with regional and global standards, guidelines, and strategic priorities. Maintain audit readiness through accurate documentation, record retention, and archiving practices in partnership with GOSC. Ensure adherence to all relevant incentive compensation policies, procedures, governance requirements, and Legal and Compliance standards, including GMIS policy application. Analytics & Strategic Consulting Analyze incentive compensation program effectiveness and identify opportunities for optimization. Generate, maintain, and communicate incentive compensation analyses, reports, dashboards, and insights to monitor program health and support business decision-making. Leverage data and analytics to identify trends, evaluate program performance, and recommend improvements aligned with market objectives. Build robust business cases for compensation plan and quota-setting enhancements, balancing motivation, affordability, and compliance. Serve as a trusted advisor to market leadership by providing objective, data-driven recommendations and solutions. Operational Excellence & Continuous Improvement Lead strategic projects and continuous improvement initiatives that enhance GOSC's value proposition, service delivery, and operational effectiveness. Proactively identify business needs and opportunities to improve existing services, processes, tools, and incentive compensation programs. Drive the adoption of best practices, innovation, and standardization across supported international markets. Work independently and lead by influence, delivering on business strategies, goals, and objectives through strong analytical, facilitation, negotiation, and stakeholder management skills. Key Success Factors The successful candidate will: Demonstrate a strong balance of analytical rigor, business acumen, and stakeholder influence. Be equally comfortable developing complex incentive compensation models and presenting recommendations to senior business leaders. Operate with a high degree of ownership, accountability, and independent judgment. Effectively manage multiple priorities across diverse international markets while maintaining attention to detail and execution excellence. Build trust through data-driven decision making, collaboration, and consistent delivery of high-quality results. Champion continuous improvement and proactively identify opportunities to enhance business value. QUALIFICATION: Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Data Science, Operations Research, Business Analytics, Economics, Finance, or a related quantitative discipline. An MBA or other advanced degree is preferred. 5-10 years of experience within the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, healthcare, or related industry, with a focus on Commercial Operations, Sales Force Effectiveness, Incentive Compensation, Business Analytics, or Process Improvement. Demonstrated experience designing, optimizing, or supporting incentive compensation programs, sales performance management processes, or other commercial operations initiatives. Proven ability to manage complex operational timelines, coordinate tasks across multiple stakeholders, and ensure delivery against critical business deadlines. Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities with experience translating complex data into actionable business insights and recommendations. Experience planning, executing, and monitoring cross-functional projects in a fast-paced and dynamic environment. Demonstrated project management skills with a track record of driving initiatives from concept through implementation. title: Senior Manager, Veeva RIM Integration Manager
jobDescription:
Role Summary: At Pfizer we make medicines and vaccines that change patients' lives with a global reach of over 780 million patients. Within Digital R&D Creation Center, the Veeva RIM team is responsible for defining the strategy and leading the delivery of the Veeva RIM product suite to end users. This includes the operation, implementation, and integration of Veeva RIM solutions that address R&D business processes effectively. At Pfizer, Veeva RIM product suite includes all modules including Registrations, HA Correspondence, Submissions & Publishing. The Snr Manager, Veeva RIM Integration Manager, is a hands-on individual contributor responsible for coordinating release readiness and lifecycle management for a complex portfolio of 60+ upstream and downstream integrations supporting Pfizer’s Veeva RIM product suite. This role combines project management, stakeholder communication, and technical integration understanding, including knowledge of the Veeva RIM data model and how data model changes impact integrations and consuming systems. The role works closely with Product Management, Business Owners, Business Process Owners, Regulatory Operations, technical teams, Quality, validation partners, integration owners, consuming application teams, and vendors to manage release impacts, data model changes, remediation needs, cutover readiness, and operational handoffs in alignment with Agile, SDLC methodologies. Role

RESPONSIBILITIES:
Integration Portfolio and Project Management • Accountable for coordinating visibility, readiness tracking, dependency management, and stakeholder alignment across a portfolio of 60+ upstream and downstream Veeva RIM integrations spanning consuming systems, business processes, data flows, and stakeholder groups. • Serve on a SAFe Agile team and contribute to PI planning, backlog refinement, sprint execution, and management of Veeva RIM release impacts, dependencies, risks, issues, readiness status, cutover activities, and operational handoffs across the integration landscape. • Accountable for ensuring downstream consumers, upstream source systems, and Business Process Owners have clear awareness of upcoming release scope, timing, data model changes, process impacts, testing expectations, cutover needs, and required actions. • Accountable for developing and managing release communications, Business Process Owner updates, consumer impact summaries, readiness checkpoints, escalation messages, and post-release follow-up. • Accountable for tracking timelines, milestones, dependencies, action items, decisions, and stakeholder status reporting to keep integration work aligned to Veeva RIM release commitments. Technical Integration and Remediation Coordination • Accountable for coordinating with integration owners, consuming application teams, technical leads, platform teams, and vendors to ensure technical issues, root causes, remediation plans, and readiness risks are visible and actively tracked. • Apply practical understanding of the Veeva RIM data model, APIs, middleware, ETL patterns, file-based integrations, SSO, data mapping, data model impacts, error handling, monitoring, and operational support to coordinate technical discussions and decisions. • Accountable for facilitating alignment with technical teams responsible for remediating impacted consuming systems to confirm readiness, track remediation progress, resolve dependencies, and support smooth cutover for Veeva RIM data model or integration changes. • Technical design and remediation activities are performed by the accountable technical teams; this role coordinates impact assessment, readiness tracking, communications, and cutover alignment across those teams. Testing, Validation, and Operational Readiness • Accountable for coordinating functional, integration, regression, user acceptance, cutover, and operational readiness testing across impacted systems and consumers. • Partner with Quality, validation, testing, engineering, consumer teams, and vendors to ensure integration changes meet SDLC and CSV expectations, including requirements traceability, test evidence, defect management, and release approvals. • Accountable for maintaining key integration and release materials, such as integration inventories, consumer impact matrices, interface specifications, data flow diagrams, release checklists, runbooks, decision logs, environment matrix and support handoff materials. Basic

QUALIFICATIONS:
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, Business, or a related field, with 7+ years of relevant experience, or equivalent combination of education and experience. Experience supporting integration delivery for enterprise platforms; experience with Veeva Vault and/or Veeva RIM integrations is strongly preferred. Experience coordinating complex integration work across upstream systems, downstream consumers, technical teams, vendors, and business stakeholder groups. Strong project management skills, including planning, milestone tracking, dependency management, risk/issue management, release readiness tracking, and stakeholder status reporting. Strong communications skills, including the ability to create clear release communications, Business Process Owner updates, consumer impact summaries, readiness updates, escalation messages, and executive-ready status updates. Practical understanding of the Veeva RIM data model and integration concepts, including APIs, middleware, ETL patterns, file-based integrations, SSO, data mapping, data model impacts, error handling, monitoring, remediation coordination, and operational support. Experience with Agile delivery, SDLC controls, release governance in a regulated environment.

Experience supporting Regulatory business processes and/or working in the Life Sciences industry. jobDescription:

Serve as solution architect and design authority for the team, defining reference architectures, technical standards, and reusable patterns across data, AI, and BI solutions, and providing technical sign-off on solution designs. jobDescription: Role Summary: An Equipment Maintenance Engineer is responsible for ensuring the optimal performance, reliability, and safety of machinery and equipment used in pharmaceutical industry. This role involves planning and executing preventive and corrective maintenance, troubleshooting equipment issues, and implementing improvements to reduce downtime and extend equipment life. Identify safety improvements. Can initiate General and LOTO permits. In-depth knowledge of specific engineering practices relevant to their field. Understanding of regulatory standards and quality control measures. Competence in applying standard engineering practices and procedures under supervision. Ability to perform routine tasks with some guidance. Knowledge of EAMS functionalities, including preventive maintenance scheduling and work order management. Initiate EAMS work order and execution independently. Comprehensive knowledge of equipment qualification standards and regulatory requirements. Ability to conduct equipment qualification tests and document results accurately. Can troubleshoot basic issues with guidance. In-depth understanding of inventory management principles. Knowledge of basic forecasting methods. Familiarity with inventory management software and tools. Ability to conduct stock counts and inventory audits. Managing reorder points and lead times Using software to track spare parts inventory Understand equipment working principle, and equipment manual Understand basic mechanical or electrical knowledge for equipment maintenance Equipment verification knowledge When find equipment error or hidden danger, stop it, can analyze, and determine simple faults and make partial adjustments Able to use professional tools like multi-meter, analyzer. Able to determine errors within operating area and outside the control cabinet. Able to carry out mechanical and electrical maintenance. Able to train operators in simple troubleshooting. Coordinate to manage consumables and spares required by own shift, check storage level. Coordinate to make maintenance plan for spares of own shift and execute the plan. Participate in equipment improvement project. With guidance from equipment suppliers and experienced engineers, conduct more comprehensive preventive maintenance beyond cleaning and lubricating. Repost, conclude and paraphrase the learning. Check and correct the work of others. Participate in deviation investigation, support problem solving. Execute per CAPA requirements. Able to follow relevant compliance requirements. Comply to relevant compliance procedures Correct self and others when finding noncompliant behaviors. Identify potential noncompliance in relevant areas and participate in improvement activities. Provide improvement suggestions and participate in implementation. Fill in the required records correctly and independently. Review and correct other’s records. Understand relevant audit requirements and prepare for them accordingly. Independently answer questions relevant to your own work correctly and provide proper evidence. Take main role in some compliance improvement work Understand relevant equipment operating SOP/WI/ cleaning / lubricating knowledge. Understand the functioning of equipment parameters. Aware of overall process and regulations about new equipment, and new process introduction. Revise or write relevant SOP/WI. Understand M1 method and tools. Understand the equivalent knowledge of yellow belt. Understand basic lean production knowledge (8 waste, 5S, visual management, standard work, continuous improvement, PDCA circle, etc.). Coordinate with others to use M1 to improve quality deviations, safety incidents, equipment performance, explore the root causes and implement effective measures. Make standard for 5S, visualization and standard work, coach relevant person to implement. Able to follow PDCA cycle for problem solving and improvement projects. Take the initiative to share with others about learning outcomes. Collaborate with operations and engineering teams to improve system reliability and performance. Ensure compliance with safety standards, industry regulations, and quality protocols. Assist in the installation and commissioning of new equipment Includes Mechanical & Instrumentation systems. Participate in audits and inspections, providing technical support and documentation as needed. Support equipment qualification and validation processes (IQ/OQ/PQ). Execution of spare parts & Inventory. Calibrate instruments such as pressure gauges, temperature sensors, flow meters, and analytical instruments. Work with PLCs, SCADA, and Microbiology systems used in pharmaceutical manufacturing. Supporting automation projects and upgrades. Knowledge of control system wirings, P&ID drawings. Collaborates effectively across teams, builds positive working relationships, demonstrates flexibility in dynamic environments, and respects cultural differences. Proactively drives personal development and supports the learning of others, leveraging knowledge to improve team performance and operational outcomes. Make timely and effective decisions in familiar situations, taking ownership for outcomes while ensuring compliance and safety. Upholds and advocates for high ethical standards, ensuring others also act with integrity while promoting a culture of trust and accountability. Recognizes and celebrates the achievements of others, shows pride in their role and team contributions, and promotes a positive and enjoyable work environment. Demonstrates a willingness to adapt to new challenges, respectfully engages in conversations, builds trust through consistent behavior, and shows basic empathy toward colleagues. Key interface to other divisions and facilitates cross-functional project modeling, resourcing and overall performance. Lead a team of subject matter experts in the development and maintenance of procedural documentation related to Pfizer clinical, medical, safety, and/or regulatory processes. title: Filling Instrumentation Engineer
jobDescription:
Use Your Power for Purpose Whether you are involved in the design and development of manufacturing processes for products or supporting maintenance and reliability, engineering is crucial to ensuring customers and patients receive the medicines they need, precisely when they need them. By collaborating with our forward-thinking engineering team, you'll play a key role in accelerating the delivery of medicines to the world. Your innovative ideas and proactive actions will help us imagine new possibilities and bring them to life, ensuring that vital medications reach those in need more swiftly and efficiently. Your contributions will be instrumental in enhancing manufacturing information systems, boosting success rates, and ensuring zero downtime. By integrating manufacturing processes, operational knowledge, equipment control, and data into cohesive systems, you will enforce seamless operations across various departments. Your dedication will be pivotal in meeting project objectives and goals, fostering a collaborative team environment, and driving your colleagues towards success.
1. Position Overview The Equipment Maintenance Engineer (J40B) plays a critical role in ensuring uninterrupted, safe, and compliant operation of pharmaceutical manufacturing assets across Upstream, Downstream, Utilites, and Fill–Finish areas. This position requires hands-on troubleshooting, preventive and predictive maintenance execution, calibration activities, documentation compliance, and participation in continuous improvement & engineering projects.
2. Detailed Responsibilities 2.1 Functional Responsibilities
- Strictly adhere to site EHS guidelines, LOTO procedures, safe work practices, and participate in hazard identification & risk assessments.
- Lead or support issuance, execution, and closure of work permits (General, LOTO, Hot Work, Height Work, Confined Space).
- Perform detailed root cause analysis for equipment failures and support CAPA development, deviation investigations, and change control documentation.
- Manage preventive maintenance plan execution in EAMS/CMMS, ensuring work orders, spare consumption, and task completion records are accurately updated.
- Monitor equipment health parameters, component wear trends, and propose predictive maintenance actions.
- Support engineering projects related to equipment upgrades, safety enhancements, automation improvements, and capacity expansions.
- Maintain 5S, workplace organization, and visual management standards across maintenance workshops and equipment areas. 2.2 Technical Responsibilities
- Conduct preventive, breakdown, and predictive maintenance for mechanical, electrical, and instrumentation systems across Solution Prep, Vial Washing, Tunnel Sterilization, Filling, Capping, Inspection, and Packaging areas.
- Calibrate field instruments including transmitters, sensors, gauges, flowmeters, control valves, and analytical instruments as per GMP procedures.
- Perform mechanical alignments, shaft coupling, lubrication, pump overhauling, pneumatic system troubleshooting, and equipment balancing.
- Troubleshoot PLC, SCADA, and DCS system–related alarms under guidance; assist in automation upgrades and FAT/SAT activities.
- Support installation, commissioning, and qualification of new equipment (IQ/OQ/PQ), ensuring documentation accuracy and compliance.
- Execute shut-down maintenance activities including equipment dismantling, inspection, refurbishment, and reassembly.
- Ensure availability and proper management of spares, consumables, and critical parts by coordinating with Stores and Procurement teams. 2.3 Behavioral Attributes
- Demonstrate strong communication skills, ensuring accurate reporting, escalation, and coordination with Operations, Quality, and Engineering teams.
- Take ownership during equipment failures, respond promptly to urgent issues, and support cross-functional troubleshooting efforts.
- Actively participate in knowledge-sharing discussions, train operators on basic troubleshooting, and mentor junior technicians.
- Support a culture of integrity, speak up when observing non-compliances, and reinforce good documentation practices.
- Maintain positive team collaboration, adaptability to dynamic manufacturing environments, and contribute to a culture of continuous improvement.
3. Essential Qualifications & Experience
- Diploma or B.Tech in Mechanical, Instrumentation, or Electronics Engineering.

title: Group Manager - Quality Control
jobDescription:
Use Your Power for Purpose Every day, everything we do is driven by an unwavering commitment to delivering safe and effective products to patients. Our quality culture, which is both science and risk-based, is flexible, innovative, and customer-oriented. Whether you are engaged in development, maintenance, compliance, or analysis through research programs, your contribution will have a direct impact on patients. Our dedication to quality and safety ensures that we consistently meet the highest standards, making a real difference in the lives of those we serve. Join us in our mission to improve patient outcomes through excellence in every aspect of our work. What You Will Achieve In this role, you will: Leadership & People Management Lead, coach, and manage Quality Control teams through goal setting, performance reviews, feedback, development planning, and succession readiness. Identify development needs, foster teamwork, inclusion, and a culture of accountability and continuous improvement. Manage workforce planning, leave management, and performance appraisal cycles. Actively share knowledge, encourage innovation, and support risk‑based decision making. Quality Control & Laboratory Operations Plan, manage, and oversee analytical activities related to: In‑process, finished product, stability, process validation, exhibit batch, market complaint, and retention sample testing Stability sample pulling, testing, protocol approval, compilation reports, and annual stability report submissions Visual inspection of retention samples per approved schedules Ensure timely review, approval, and completion of all QC activities in alignment with site KPIs. Review and approve, Laboratory investigations, QC documentation including raw data, protocols, reports, and SOPs in compliance with c GMP. Equipment Qualification, Calibration & Lifecycle Management Ensure equipment qualification and lifecycle compliance for QC laboratory instruments, including IQ/OQ/PQ activities. Oversee calibration, preventive maintenance, and requalification of QC equipment in accordance with approved schedules and regulatory requirements. Ensure Equipment Qualification protocols, reports, deviations, and change controls are reviewed and approved. Collaborate with Engineering, Validation, and QA to support: New equipment introduction Decommissioning and replacement activities Qualification impact assessments for changes Ensure data integrity, ALCOA+ principles, and computerized system compliance for analytical instrumentation. Stability Management Approve and manage stability and retention sample requests, protocols, reports, and annual submissions. Ensure sponsor‑site stability samples, review of shipment temperature excursions, and execution of stability studies at site. Ensure PRQ and qualification of stability chambers as per approved schedules. Compliance, Audits & Quality Systems Ensure alignment with c GMP, regulatory requirements, and Pfizer Quality Standards across all QC activities. Represent CQ during internal, external, customer, and regulatory audits and inspections. Support timely investigation and closure of Incidents, Deviations, CAPAs, and Change Controls, including cross‑functional impact assessments. Ensure personnel safety, safe material handling, and adherence to EHS requirements within QC laboratories. Continuous Improvement & Technical Excellence Guide analysts in the application of continuous improvement tools such as standard work, visual management, LEAN, and Six Sigma methodologies. Drive simplification, digitization, and efficiency improvement initiatives across CQ processes. Provide technical expertise in troubleshooting analytical methods, instruments, and laboratory issues. Support method transfers from R&D to QC and ensure readiness for routine testing. Collaboration & Business Partnership Partner with Manufacturing, QA, Engineering, R&D, Supply Chain, and external customers to support site objectives and timelines. Establish and monitor departmental performance metrics to drive operational effectiveness. Communicate complex technical concepts clearly, solicit feedback, and influence stakeholders using sound scientific and business rationale. Here Is What You Need (Minimum Requirements)

EDUCATION:
B. Pharm / M. Pharm / M.Sc. Experience: Minimum 10+ years of pharmaceutical industry experience with a strong background in Quality Control. Extensive knowledge of c GMP compliance for Quality Control laboratories, including, testing, stability management, lab investigations, equipment qualification, and data integrity. Demonstrated experience in: Analytical testing, stability management, and retention samples Equipment qualification, calibration, and maintenance oversight Audit handling and regulatory inspections Incident, CAPA, Change Control management People leadership and performance management Proficiency in a wide range of analytical techniques and QC instrumentation. Bonus Points If You Have (Preferred Requirements) Master's degree Knowledge in the application of statistical tools, root cause analysis, and/or six sigma methodologies Experience with environmental testing, utility monitoring, analytical testing, microbial identification, and sterility testing Expertise in QC instrumentation, qualification, and troubleshooting Experience in setting requirements for the transfer of methodology from Research and Development (R&D) Ability to manage projects and ongoing work activities of moderate complexity Excellent verbal and written communication skills Ability to foster teamwork and colleague development Experience using common AI tools, including generative technologies such as Chat GPT or Microsoft Copilot, to support problem solving and enhance productivity. Demonstrated curiosity for exploring how these tools can improve outcomes and understanding of responsible AI practices, including risk management and ethical use Work Location Assignment: On Premise Pfizer is an equal opportunity employer and complies with all applicable equal employment opportunity legislation in each jurisdiction in which it operates. What You Will Achieve In this role, you will: Contribute to moderately complex projects, managing time effectively to meet targets. Apply skills and knowledge to contribute to team efforts. Use judgment to modify methods and techniques as needed. Monitor and complete periodic reviews, including the validation master plan for automation engineering. Demonstrate exceptional planning, organizing, time management, and team participation skills. Take responsibility for routine and preventive maintenance, ensuring equipment and facilities operate safely and efficiently. Here Is What You Need (Minimum Requirements) Key Responsibilities Automation Responsibilities Configure, maintain, and troubleshoot Emerson Delta V DCS systems. Develop and modify control modules, equipment modules, phases, and batch logic. Design and maintain Delta V operator graphics, alarms, trends, and reports. Support DCS upgrades, migrations, patch management, and lifecycle activities. Perform system backups, restoration, and disaster recovery activities. Optimize control strategies to improve process performance, quality, and productivity. Integrate Delta V systems with PLCs, SCADA, Historians, and third-party systems. Ensure compliance with cybersecurity and automation standards. Instrumentation Responsibilities Monitor and maintain field instruments such as pressure, temperature, flow, level, analytical instruments, and control valves. Support installation, testing, and commissioning of new instrumentation systems. Coordinate with maintenance and operations teams for instrument reliability improvements. Diagnose communication issues related to HART, Foundation Fieldbus, Profibus, Modbus, and other industrial protocols. Support control valve diagnostics and performance assessment. Participate in plant projects involving instrumentation and automation upgrades. Ensure instrumentation systems comply with safety, quality, and regulatory requirements. Manage instrument spares, technical specifications, and vendor interactions. title: Cyber & Infrastructure Technology Senior Analyst
jobDescription: Purpose of the Role / Role Summary The Cyber & Infrastructure Technology Senior Analyst drives and contributes to the secure, stable, and compliant operation of Digital and Automation infrastructure within the manufacturing environment. The role focuses on coordinating and executing cybersecurity, network, and infrastructure activities in line with established standards and governance to protect critical digital assets and ensure reliable plant operations. The Team Member performs day‑to‑day operations, lifecycle, and support activities across cybersecurity and network domains ensuring resilient, secure, and optimized Digital and Automation systems. The role works closely with the Cyber Security & Network Lead, the global Cyber Security Team and cross‑functional partners to support secure infrastructure operations, incident response, and continuous improvement at site level. The Cyber & Infrastructure Technology Senior Analyst provides technical guidance within defined scope and contributes to improving cybersecurity and infrastructure practices, escalating where required. Role Description Responsibilities Governance, Regulations & Standards Execute all work in alignment with applicable quality, cybersecurity, and regulatory requirements; follow established SOPs and governance processes; identify and escalate deviations or risks as required. Support inspections, audits, and assessments by providing accurate documentation, data, and technical input when requested. Coordinate and contribute to cybersecurity regulations and standards application, enhancing deployment and adherence across assigned systems. Architecture, Controls & Cybersecurity Delivery Execute defined site-level cybersecurity and network activities in accordance with established Digital and Automation architecture, cybersecurity, and network standards. Enhance implementation and effectiveness of approved control strategies and tools to maintain secure and compliant Digital and Automation environments. Contribute to vulnerability remediation activities and improving control effectiveness and risk mitigation approaches. Enhance cybersecurity planning, monitoring, and control tools by providing technical input, execution feedback, and documentation in line with approved strategies and standards. Participate in local or global cybersecurity, infrastructure, and Digital & Automation–related projects as an executing team member. Operations, Monitoring & Lifecycle Optimize day-to-day Digital and Automation infrastructure operations, including proactive monitoring, incident handling, and issue resolution for assigned systems and network components as well as user management and audit trail reviews. Maintain accurate asset and configuration inventory records for assigned Digital and Automation systems and network components; ensure updates are performed in a timely manner to support lifecycle, cybersecurity, and inspection readiness. Support change management activities for infrastructure and cybersecurity changes, including impact assessments, documentation updates, and coordination with relevant stakeholders. Execute and improve software and hardware lifecycle delivery, (e.g. patching, upgrades, and end-of-life tasks) following approved plans and change management processes. Optimize OT & IT infrastructure and architecture execution and infrastructure monitoring practices. Incident, Crisis & Business Continuity Troubleshoot and support incident, deviation, and recovery activities and escalations to enable secure and return-to-service in accordance to agreed SLAs while maintaining data integrity and validated state control. Support business continuity readiness by helping maintain recovery procedures/playbooks for assigned services and infrastructure and participating in recovery/failover testing or continuity drills as required. Contribute to improving crisis response and business continuity effectiveness. PANS Support Support PANS-related activities by executing defined monitoring, configuration validation, and data collection tasks, escalating deviations per governance. Execute assigned PANS remediation activities (e.g. configuration corrections, rule updates, device/network changes, or control implementation) in accordance with approved remediation plans, change management processes, and site/governance standards. Sustain and improve PANS operations through proactive monitoring and issue resolution. Key Attributes, Skills & Competencies Strong knowledge of cybersecurity principles, network concepts, and OT/IT integration within regulated manufacturing (Digital and Automation environments). Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to assess impact, troubleshoot effectively, and escalate appropriately. Ability to follow formal change control and documentation/evidence practices in regulated/validated environments. Understands, explores and applies monitoring and troubleshooting methods to identify common network/infrastructure issues and support timely resolution. Drives accountability and ownership for assigned work and delivers reliably within agreed scope, priorities, and timelines. Provides guidance and collaborates effectively within the Cyber Security & Network Services team and with cross-functional partners, following defined governance and escalation pathways. Able to support incidents and recovery activities in a structured manner, maintaining clear communication and composure under time pressure. Supports a culture of professionalism, security awareness, continuous improvement, and personal development through day-to-day behaviors. Supports and mentors team members in cybersecurity and infrastructure practices. Preferred Qualifications, Experience & Certifications Bachelor’s degree or equivalent qualification in Engineering, Computer Science, Information Systems, Cybersecurity, Automation, or related technical field. 3+ years of experience in Digital and Automation infrastructure, OT/IT environments, network operations, or cybersecurity in an industrial and/or regulated manufacturing environment. Practical experience supporting cybersecurity controls, networked systems, or infrastructure within validated or compliance-driven environments (e.g., pharma, biotech, or regulated manufacturing). Familiarity with infrastructure lifecycle activities (patching, upgrades, vulnerability remediation, end-of-life) under defined governance processes. Experience working within formal change management, deviation, and incident response processes; exposure to business continuity testing/drills is a plus. Exposure to plant network environments and manufacturing automation systems (OT networking) is preferred. Relevant training or certifications is preferred (e.g., networking, cybersecurity fundamentals, ITIL, or vendor-specific technical certifications This Role will support four sites: Wuxi, Dalian, Goa and Jakarta.
